source_text: Τιμόθεον ἔγραψεν· «οὐ γὰρ ἔδωκεν ὑμῖν ὁ θεὸς πνεῦμα δουλείας, ἀλλὰ πνεῦμα δυνάμεως καὶ ἀγάπης καὶ σωφρονισμοῦ», καὶ πρὸς Ῥωμαίους· «παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ διὰ ἀγάπης τοῦ πνεύματος», καὶ ἑτέρωθι· «ὁ δὲ καρπὸς τοῦ πνεύματός ἐστιν ἀγάπη, χαρά, εἰρήνη,» 3.7 ὅμοιον τῷ. «ὁ θεὸς ἀγάπη ἐστίν,» καὶ τῷ· «μετέστησεν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ υἱοῦ τῆς ἀγάπης αὐτοῦ·» καί· «καθὼς ὁ Χριστὸς ἠγάπησεν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν,» καὶ πάλιν· «τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ἀγαπήσαντός με,» ὅμοιον καὶ τῷ· «ἀπάρτι ὄψεσθε τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καθήμενον ἐκ δεξιῶν τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ πατρός,» καὶ τῷ· «ἐγὼ ἔγνων δύναμιν ἐξελθοῦσαν ἐξ ἐμοῦ.» 3.8 πνεῦμα σοφίας καὶ συνέσεως, πνεῦμα βουλῆς καὶ ἰσχύος, πνεῦμα γνώσεως καὶ εὐσεβείας· πνεῦμα φόβου θεοῦ, πνεῦμα κρίσεως καὶ καύσεως, ὡς Ἡσαῖας προφητεύει· καὶ ὡς ἡ σοφία λέγει· «φιλάνθρωπον γὰρ πνεῦμα σοφίας,» καὶ ὡς Μωυσῆς ἐν τῇ Ἐξόδῳ διηγεῖται· «ἰδοὺ ἀνακέκληκεν ὁ θεὸς ἐξ ὀνόματος τὸν Βεσελεὴλ τὸν τοῦ Οὐρί, τὸν τοῦ Ὤρ, ἐκ φυλῆς Ἰούδα, καὶ ἐνέπλησεν αὐτὸν πνεῦμα θεῖον σοφίας καὶ συνέσεως καὶ ἐπιστήμης,» καὶ κατὰ τὸν Βαρούχ· «ἐγκατέλιπες τὴν πηγὴν τῆς σοφίας», καὶ ὡς αἱ παροιμίαι διδάσκουσιν· «ὁ θεὸς τῇ σοφίᾳ ἐθεμελίωσεν τὴν γῆν, ἡτοίμασεν δὲ οὐ ρανοὺς ἐν φρονήσει,» καθὰ περὶ τοῦ θεοῦ πατρὸς Ἡσαῖας εἶπεν· «αὐτὸς σοφὸς ἦγεν ἐπ' αὐτοὺς κακά». περὶ δὲ τοῦ μονογενοῦς Παῦλος ἔφη· «Χριστός, θεοῦ δύναμις, καὶ θεοῦ σοφία·» καὶ ἄλλος· «εὐλογήσω τὸν κύριον τὸν συνετίσαντά με.» 3.9 πνεῦμα πραότητος, καθὰ Παῦλος νουθετεῖ Γαλάτας· «ἀδελφοί, ἐὰν καὶ προληφθῇ ἄνθρωπος ἔν τινι παραπτώματι, ὑμεῖς οἱ πνευματικοὶ καταρτίζετε τὸν τοιοῦτον ἐν πνεύ ματι πραότητος.» 3.10 πνεῦμα παιδείας, τουτέστι σοφίας. ἡ γὰρ σοφία λέγει· «πνεῦμα παιδείας φεύξεται δόλον, καὶ ἀπαναστήσεται ἀπὸ λογισμῶν ἀσυνέτων.» 3.11 πνεῦμα υἱοθεσίας, ὡς Παῦλος τὸ πρῶτον Ῥωμαίοις ἀπέστειλεν· «ὅσοι γὰρ πνεύματι θεοῦ ἄγονται, οὗτοι υἱοὶ θεοῦ εἰσιν. ὅτι γὰρ ἐλάβετε πνεῦμα υἱοθεσίας, ἐν ᾧ κράζομεν· Ἀββὰ ὁ πατήρ, αὐτὸ τὸ πνεῦμα συμμαρτυρεῖ τῷ πνεύματι ἡμῶν, ὅτι ἐσμὲν τέκνα θεοῦ.» 3.12 πνεῦμα ἐπαγγελίας, κατὰ τὸν αὐτὸν ἀπόστολον Ἐφεσίοις γράφοντα· «ἐν ᾧ καὶ πιστεύσαντες, ἐσφραγίσθητε τῷ πνεύματι τῆς ἐπαγγελίας τῷ ἁγίῳ, ὅς ἐστιν ἀρραβὼν τῆς κληρονομίας ἡμῶν,» καὶ πρὸς Γαλάτας· «Χριστὸς ἡμᾶς ἐξηγόρασεν ἐκ τῆς κατάρας τοῦ νόμου, γενό μενος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν κατάρα. γέγραπται γάρ· ἐπικατάρατος πᾶς ὁ κρεμάμενος ἐπὶ ξύλου· ἵνα εἰς τὰ ἔθνη ἡ εὐλογία τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ γένηται ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, ἵνα τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ πνεύματος λάβωμεν διὰ τῆς πίστεως.» 3.13 πνεῦμα πίστεως καὶ ἀποκαλύψεως, κατὰ τὸν αὐτὸν Κορινθίοις· δηλοῦντα ἐν τῇ δευτέρᾳ ἐπιστολῇ· «ἔχοντες δὲ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα τῆς πίστεως», καὶ πάλιν· «ἡμῖν δὲ ὁ θεὸς ἀπεκάλυψεν διὰ πνεύματος αὐτοῦ.» ὅμοιον οὖν ᾧ Ῥωμαίοις ἐδήλωσεν· «πιστὸς ὁ θεός, δι' οὗ ἐκλήθητε εἰς κοινωνίαν τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ», καὶ τῷ ὑπὸ Μωυσέως ἐν τῷ δευτερονομίῳ λεχθέντι· «καὶ γνώσῃ σήμερον, ὅτι κύριος ὁ θεός σου, οὗτος θεὸς ὁ θεὸς ὁ πιστός,» καὶ τῷ ψάλλοντι· «πιστὸς κύριος ἐν πᾶσιν τοῖς λόγοις αὐτοῦ καὶ ὅσιος ἐν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτοῦ.» 3.14 πνεῦμα ἡγεμονικόν, πνεῦμα εὐθὲς κατὰ τὸν ∆αυὶδ ἐν τῷ νʹ ἐξομολογούμενον· «πνεύματι ἡγεμονικῷ στήρισόν με»· ὁμοίως τῷ ψάλλοντι ἐν λβʹ· «ὅτι εὐθὴς ὁ λόγος τοῦ κυρίου καὶ πάντα τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ ἐν πίστει», καὶ τῷ Μωυσεῖ λέγοντι· «εὐθὴς κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἀδικία ἐν αὐτῷ.» 3.15 πνεῦμα χάριτος, καθὰ ὁ ἀπόστολος Ἑβραίοις ἐπιστέλλει· «ὁ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καταπατήσας καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς χάριτος ἐνυβρίσας,» καὶ γὰρ ὁ αὐτὸς ἔγραψεν περὶ μὲν τοῦ πατρός· «χάριτι θεοῦ εἰμί, ὅ εἰμι 47 καὶ ἡ χάρις αὐτοῦ ἡ εἰς ἐμέ,» περὶ δὲ τοῦ υἱοῦ· «ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ
pass_a_gloss: [Continuing: as Paul in the second letter to] Timothy wrote: 'For God did not give you a spirit of slavery, but a spirit of power and of love and of self-control', and to the Romans: 'And I exhort you, brothers, through our Lord Jesus Christ and through the love of the Spirit', and in another place: 'But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace'. 3.7 This is like the saying: 'God is love', and the saying: 'he moved [us] over into the kingdom of the Son of his love'; and: 'just as Christ loved the church', and again: 'of the Son of God who loved me'; like also the saying: 'from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right of the power of the Father', and the saying: 'I knew power having gone out from me'. 3.8 Spirit of wisdom and understanding, spirit of counsel and strength, spirit of knowledge and godliness; spirit of the fear of God, spirit of judgment and burning, as Isaiah prophesies; and as Wisdom says: 'for a spirit of wisdom is loving toward mankind', and as Moses narrates in Exodus: 'Behold, God has called up by name Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, out of the tribe of Judah, and he filled him with a divine spirit of wisdom and understanding and knowledge', and according to Baruch: 'you have left behind the spring of wisdom', and as the Proverbs teach: 'God by wisdom founded the earth, and he made ready the heavens in prudence', just as Isaiah said about God the Father: 'he, being wise, brought evils upon them'. And about the only-begotten Paul said: 'Christ, power of God and wisdom of God'; and another: 'I will bless the Lord who gave me understanding'. 3.9 Spirit of gentleness, just as Paul admonishes the Galatians: 'Brothers, if a man is even overtaken in some trespass, you, the spiritual ones, set such a one right in a spirit of gentleness'. 3.10 Spirit of instruction, that is, of wisdom. For Wisdom says: 'a spirit of instruction will flee deceit, and will rise up and go away from senseless reasonings'. 3.11 Spirit of adoption as sons, as Paul first sent to the Romans: 'For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are sons of God. For that you received a spirit of adoption, in which we cry out: Abba, the Father, the Spirit itself bears witness together with our spirit that we are children of God'. 3.12 Spirit of promise, according to the same apostle writing to the Ephesians: 'in whom also, having believed, you were sealed with the Holy Spirit of the promise, who is the pledge of our inheritance', and to the Galatians: 'Christ bought us out from the curse of the law, having become a curse on our behalf. For it is written: Accursed is everyone who hangs upon wood; in order that the blessing of Abraham might come to the nations in Christ Jesus, in order that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith'. 3.13 Spirit of faith and of revelation, according to the same apostle making plain to the Corinthians in the second letter: 'and having the same spirit of faith', and again: 'but to us God revealed through his Spirit'. This is like, then, what he made plain to the Romans: 'Faithful is God, through whom you were called into the fellowship of his Son', and the thing said by Moses in Deuteronomy: 'and you will know today that the Lord your God, this one is God, the faithful God', and the one singing psalms: 'Faithful is the Lord in all his words and holy in all his works'. 3.14 Governing spirit, upright spirit, according to David confessing in the fiftieth [Greek numbering, English fifty-first Psalm]: 'with a governing spirit make me firm'; likewise the one singing in the thirty-second [English thirty-third]: 'for upright is the word of the Lord and all his works are in faithfulness', and Moses saying: 'upright is the Lord our God and there is no unrighteousness in him'. 3.15 Spirit of grace, just as the apostle writes by letter to the Hebrews: 'he who trampled down the Son of God and insulted the Spirit of grace'; for indeed the same one wrote about the Father: 'by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace that is toward me', and about the Son: 'the grace of our Lord Jesus [the sentence continues in the next section]'.
pass_b_english: … Timothy, wrote: “For God did not give you a spirit of slavery, but a spirit of power and of love and of self-control” (2 Timothy 1:7); and to the Romans: “I appeal to you, brothers, through our Lord Jesus Christ and through the love of the Spirit” (Romans 15:30); and elsewhere: “But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace” (Galatians 5:22).

This is like the saying “God is love” (1 John 4:8), and “He brought us over into the kingdom of the Son of his love” (Colossians 1:13); and “just as Christ loved the church” (Ephesians 5:25); and again, “the Son of God, who loved me” (Galatians 2:20). It is like, too, the saying “From now on you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of the power of the Father” (Matthew 26:64), and “I knew that power had gone out from me” (Luke 8:46).

He is the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and strength, the Spirit of knowledge and godliness, the Spirit of the fear of God (Isaiah 11:2-3), the Spirit of judgment and of burning (Isaiah 4:4), as Isaiah prophesies. So too Wisdom says, “For the spirit of wisdom is a lover of mankind” (Wisdom of Solomon 1:6). And Moses relates in Exodus: “See, God has called by name Bezalel, the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and has filled him with a divine spirit of wisdom and understanding and knowledge” (Exodus 31:2-3). And in Baruch: “You have forsaken the fountain of wisdom” (Baruch 3:12). And as the Proverbs teach: “God by wisdom founded the earth, and by understanding he prepared the heavens” (Proverbs 3:19). In the same way Isaiah said of God the Father, “He in his wisdom brought evils upon them” (Isaiah 31:2); and of the Only-begotten Paul said, “Christ, the power of God and the wisdom of God” (1 Corinthians 1:24); and another says, “I will bless the Lord, who gave me understanding” (Psalm 16:7).

He is the Spirit of gentleness, as Paul admonishes the Galatians: “Brothers, if anyone is caught in some trespass, you who are spiritual should restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness” (Galatians 6:1).
He is the Spirit of instruction, that is, of wisdom. For Wisdom says: “The spirit of instruction will flee from deceit, and will rise and depart from senseless thoughts” (Wisdom of Solomon 1:5).

He is the Spirit of adoption, as Paul first wrote to the Romans: “For all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God. For you received the spirit of adoption, in whom we cry, ‘Abba, Father’; the Spirit himself bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God” (Romans 8:14-16).

He is the Spirit of promise, as the same apostle says when he writes to the Ephesians: “In him you also, when you believed, were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise, who is the pledge of our inheritance” (Ephesians 1:13-14); and to the Galatians: “Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us, for it is written, ‘Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree’, so that in Christ Jesus the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles, so that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith” (Galatians 3:13-14).

He is the Spirit of faith and of revelation, as the same apostle shows the Corinthians in the second letter: “Since we have the same spirit of faith” (2 Corinthians 4:13); and again: “But God has revealed it to us through his Spirit” (1 Corinthians 2:10). This is like what he made plain to the Romans: “God is faithful, by whom you were called into the fellowship of his Son” (1 Corinthians 1:9); and like what Moses said in Deuteronomy: “And you shall know today that the Lord your God, he is God, the faithful God” (Deuteronomy 7:9); and like the psalmist: “The Lord is faithful in all his words, and holy in all his works” (Psalm 144:13 LXX).

He is the governing Spirit, the upright Spirit, as David says in his confession in the fifty-first Psalm: “Establish me with a governing spirit” (Psalm 51:12). So too the psalmist in the thirty-third: “For the word of the Lord is upright, and all his works are done in faithfulness” (Psalm 33:4); and Moses, when he says, “The Lord our God is upright, and there is no unrighteousness in him” (Psalm 92:15).

He is the Spirit of grace, as the apostle writes to the Hebrews: “He who has trampled underfoot the Son of God and outraged the Spirit of grace” (Hebrews 10:29). choices.issue: Draft with wrong references, edition numbers and a broken paragraph
choices.choice: Retranslated the whole section from the Greek. The old English printed edition numbers 3.12-3.15, broke 3.11 with a dash across two paragraphs, used abbreviated references (Rom, Eph, Gal, 1 Cor, Deut, Ps, Heb), called the Greek fiftieth and thirty-second Psalms the '4th' and '122nd', cited Baruch 3:9 for 3:12, Mark 14:62 where the wording ('from now on') is Matthew 26:64, Deuteronomy 32:4 where the words are Psalm 92:15, and Psalm 145:13 for a line the KJV lacks; it made 'elsewhere' into 'to the Galatians', rendered Isaiah 31:2 as 'He was wise in doing evil against them', gave 'the promised Holy Spirit' where the title is 'the Spirit of promise', and left Isaiah 11:2-3, Isaiah 4:4, Wisdom 1:5 and 1:6 and Ephesians 1:14 unreferenced.

choices.why: The section opens mid-sentence; 'as Paul in the second letter to' ends the previous section. Only this section's words are translated, with a leading ellipsis.
The copy-text reads 'you' where the New Testament has 'us'; translated as it stands.
Didymus does not name the Galatians here; the old draft supplied it.

choices.english: He brought us over into the kingdom
choices.why: Didymus quotes Colossians 1:13 without its object; English needs one, taken from the verse itself.
Didymus adds 'of the Father' to the Gospel words to show power named of the Father; kept. 'From now on' marks Matthew 26:64.
Didymus pairs each title of the Spirit with the same word used of the Father and the Son; English says so once per group.
The Greek lists titles without a verb; 'He is' is added once at the head of each title so each reads as a sentence.

choices.english: For the spirit of wisdom is a lover of mankind
choices.why: The copy-text has σοφίας (of wisdom) where Wisdom 1:6 reads σοφία (wisdom is a kindly spirit); translated as Didymus has it, since he cites it for the title 'spirit of wisdom'.

choices.term: αὐτὸς σοφὸς ἦγεν ἐπ' αὐτοὺς κακά
choices.english: He in his wisdom brought evils upon them
choices.why: Isaiah 31:2: God, being wise, brought evils on them; the old 'He was wise in doing evil' misread it.
παιδεία can be 'discipline' or 'instruction'; Didymus glosses it as wisdom, so 'instruction'.

choices.term: ὡς Παῦλος τὸ πρῶτον Ῥωμαίοις ἀπέστειλεν
choices.english: as Paul first wrote to the Romans
choices.why: 'First' kept as ambiguous as the Greek (Romans stands first among Paul's letters).

choices.english: For you received the spirit of adoption
choices.why: The copy-text shortens Romans 8:15 ('not a spirit of slavery … but a spirit of adoption') and reads ὅτι; rendered as a plain statement of the verse.

choices.english: in the fifty-first Psalm … in the thirty-third
choices.why: Greek Psalm numbers 50 and 32 converted to English numbering (51 and 33), checked by verse text.
ἡγεμονικός is the ruling, guiding power; KJV's 'free spirit' follows the Hebrew, not Didymus' Greek.
The words are Psalm 92:15 (Greek 91:16); Didymus names Moses, which is kept. Deuteronomy 32:4 listed as a possible allusion.

choices.term: ὅμοιον οὖν ᾧ Ῥωμαίοις ἐδήλωσεν · «πιστὸς ὁ θεός …»
choices.english: what he made plain to the Romans … (1 Corinthians 1:9)
choices.why: The quoted words are 1 Corinthians 1:9; Didymus names the Romans, which is kept; see problems.

choices.term: πνεύ ματι, γενό μενος, ἐν ἁγιασ μῷ, οὐ ρανούς; 47
choices.why: Line-break splits in the copy-text joined; 47 is a printed page number, page debris.
The quotation breaks off at the end of the section and continues in the next; ended with an ellipsis.
